observation.visible_scene: An outdoor waterfront amphitheater on a clear day. A white arched canopy pavilion on angled pillars atop stone bases sits in the mid-ground, backed by a large red-brick building with a tall tower block and a curved glass facade. A calm pond fills the foreground, holding a tilted green sign that reads "No Thanks, We just ate. Please don't feed the birds." Trees and lower brick buildings line the left bank; grassy terraced steps and a small outfall pipe appear on the right. A few people stand near the pavilion.
visible_changes: The camera executes a slow, continuous pan to the left (with a slight widening/zoom-out feel): over the segment every fixed element drifts rightward within the frame. The green sign moves from left-of-center toward the center, and the pavilion and brick tower shift from centered toward the right edge.

As the view pans left, more of the left bank is revealed frame by frame: additional trees, the full rocky shoreline curving into the water at lower-left, and a lamppost at the far-left edge appear, none of which were visible at the start.

The standing figures near the pavilion (e.g., the person in white by the right stone base) keep their positions relative to the structure, confirming the apparent motion is camera-driven rather than object-driven.
Water-surface reflections shimmer subtly between frames; the structures, sign, and foliage otherwise remain static.
uncertain_details: The exact camera operation is ambiguous (pan-left vs. pan-left combined with a slight pull-back/zoom-out); only the net rightward drift of scene content and the growing left-edge reveal are certain.
Whether any small motion exists in the trees or the people is not resolvable at this sampling rate; they appear stationary.
The segment's endpoints are arbitrary crops, so the pan's start and intended end lie outside the clip.
